title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (letter to Tate, May 1966, §1.12). k is a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k), K = Frac W, and S is smooth over k. The previous page showed that crystals of coherent modules on S/W are compatible systems (M_n) of stratified modules on local lifts S_n/W_n.

Case where S lifts to X proper and smooth over R = Spec W. By the comparison theorem (EGA III 4,5), crystals of coherent modules on S are equivalent to coherent O_X-modules with a stratification relative to W. In modern terms these are modules with an integrable connection, topologically quasi-nilpotent mod p, i.e. an HPD stratification. Passing to the generic fibre X_K gives a 'localisation' functor from crystals to coherent stratified modules on X_K. Such modules are locally free, and since char K = 0 they are just vector bundles with integrable connection.

The bracketed passage on this page:
1. Suppose X_K is geometrically connected and K embeds in C. Then flat bundles on X_K correspond to representations of π_1^top(X_C^an). This uses GAGA because X is proper.
2. If π_1^top is trivial, every flat bundle on X_C is trivial. By descent C → K (horizontal sections give a K-form), every flat bundle on X_K is trivial.
3. Translated back: every coherent crystal on S is isogenous to a constant crystal, i.e. the pull-back of a crystal on k given by a finitely generated W-module.
4. By rigidity of crystals, every coherent p-crystal (F-crystal) and every bi-crystal of given weight (e.g. Dieudonné crystals) is isogenous to a trivial one. The Frobenius becomes a horizontal map between constant isocrystals and so comes from k.
5. Grothendieck calls this a 'transcendental approach' to families of formal groups in characteristic p.

Isocrystals. The functor induces a fully faithful functor from isocrystals on S to flat bundles on X_K. This works because X is proper, so Hom(M,N)⊗Q = Hom(M_K,N_K), and horizontality is preserved. He asks for the essential image and whether the functor is an equivalence. He finds this 'a bit too optimistic'. A later handwritten marginal note says 'effectivement, ça ne marche pas!'. A priori, the condition on a flat bundle should be local at the points of X that are maximal in S, i.e. the generic points of the special fibre. These are the codimension-1 points of X lying over the closed point, whose local rings are DVRs.

Formal case. If S only lifts to a formal scheme X over Spf W, then crystals of coherent modules are equivalent, essentially trivially, to coherent modules on X with stratification relative to Spf W. The next page continues by passing to the rigid generic fibre, which anticipates convergent isocrystals.
errors: No substantive error. The claim that every crystal is 'isogenous to a constant crystal' must be read in the isogeny category, where torsion crystals become zero. Under the stated hypotheses it is correct: the horizontal sections of M over X form a finitely generated W-module whose tensor with K has full rank, giving a map from a constant crystal to M that becomes an isomorphism after inverting p.
The hypotheses (proper smooth lift over W, K embeddable in C, X_C topologically simply connected) are much stronger than needed. Grothendieck does not say this, but they make the argument immediate.

The hesitation about the isocrystal-to-connection functor being an equivalence is justified, and the marginal note confirms it fails. Example: on a lifted elliptic curve, the trivial bundle with connection d + aω for |a| ≥ 1 has horizontal sections exp(-a·log_formal-group), which do not converge on residue discs. So it does not come from an isocrystal; the essential image is the convergent connections.

ideas.what: Coherent crystals on S equal stratified coherent modules on a proper smooth lift X/W (via EGA III formal comparison). On the formal lift, crystals equal modules with quasi-nilpotent integrable connection.
ideas.modern_name: Crystals on a smooth lift as modules with (HPD) integrable connection; Berthelot's crystalline–de Rham dictionary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1966/68); Berthelot (1974); Berthelot–Ogus (1978)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968); letter to Tate is cited in Berthelot's work

ideas.what: Localisation functor from (iso)crystals on S to flat bundles on the char-0 generic fibre X_K; fully faithful on isocrystals; the question of its essential image.
ideas.modern_name: Specialisation of isocrystals to the generic fibre; convergent isocrystals as the essential image (rigid version)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Tate 1966 (circulated); not in Crystals… as far as known

ideas.what: Transcendental approach: if X_C is topologically simply connected, every coherent crystal and every F-crystal / Dieudonné crystal on S is isogenous to a constant one, with consequences for families of formal / p-divisible groups.
ideas.modern_name: Triviality of (F-)isocrystals on simply connected varieties; precursor of de Jong's conjecture (isocrystals on simply connected smooth projective varieties are constant)
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Jong (conjecture); Esnault–Shiho (2018, 'Convergent isocrystals on simply connected varieties'); Esnault–Mehta for the char-p analogue of Gieseker's conjecture

ideas.what: The condition for a flat bundle on X_K to come from an isocrystal should be local at the generic points of the special fibre (DVR local rings of X at maximal points of S).
ideas.modern_name: Generic-point / generic radius of convergence criteria for convergence (Dwork transfer; Ogus; Kedlaya)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dwork, Christol–Dwork; Ogus 1984; Kedlaya (generic radius of convergence)

missed.claim: Grothendieck already in 1966 formulates a transcendental proof scheme: lift to W, pass to X_K ⊂ X_C, use π_1^top = 1 to trivialise flat bundles, then descend back to show crystals and F-crystals are isogenous to constant ones. This is exactly the strategy behind later work on de Jong's conjecture (Esnault–Shiho) for isocrystals on simply connected varieties. He also explicitly links it to the study of families of formal groups in characteristic p.
missed.quote: On voit donc là un principe d'approche transcendante pour l'étude des familles de groupes formels (par exemple) en caractéristique p
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This places the origin of the 'isocrystals on simply connected varieties are constant' circle of ideas in Grothendieck's 1966 letter. It also suggests the application, via de Jong's full faithfulness, that p-divisible groups over such S are isogenous to constant ones. This may not be credited to him in the modern literature.

missed.claim: Determining the essential image of isocrystals among flat bundles on X_K, together with the guess that the condition is local at the generic points of the special fibre. This was left open and is answered later by convergent isocrystals and generic-radius criteria. The marginal note records Grothendieck's own later recognition that the naive equivalence fails.
missed.quote: la condition cherchée sur un Module stratifié doit être de nature locale en les points de X qui sont maximaux dans S. [marg.] effectivement, ça ne marche pas !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for posing the convergence problem, and an early intuition of checking convergence at the generic points of the special fibre. It is mostly absorbed by the work of Ogus, Berthelot and Kedlaya, so there is little mathematical novelty today.

deep.surprise_reason: The letter to Tate is known to specialists and its crystal–connection dictionary is standard. The anticipations recorded here are a notable but not shocking historical detail: the transcendental argument for constancy of F-crystals on simply connected lifts (a precursor of de Jong's conjecture), the posed essential-image problem with a locality-at-generic-points guess, and the later marginal admission that it fails.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: the typed 'conn[ex]ion' is a correction of a typo ('connion' → 'connexion'), not a replacement of 'conn' by 'ex'; read 'module cohérent à connexion intégrable'.
Marginal handwritten note in the left margin next to 'trop optimiste' (which is underlined with a wavy line) reads 'effectivement, ça ne marche pas !'.
'Quand à la notion' is Grothendieck's spelling (for 'Quant à').
Handwritten page numbers: '12' top right and '13' bottom left. The square brackets around 'Enfin … caractéristique p ...' are handwritten editorial marks.
'(complexes)' is a handwritten insertion with a check mark in the right margin; 'facilement' is circled by hand.
